newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Metrobank enlivens market.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Metrobank enlivens market.

text.p: Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co enlivened an otherwise lacklustre debt market on Friday with a US$140 million five-year FRCD.
Bankers said Metrobank was taking advantage of lower funding costs.
Its all-in for top-tier managers was 74 basis points, compared to 95 basis points for Metrobank's US$50 million five-year FRCD in August 1996, they said.
Credit rating upgrades of the Philippines by both Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's also helped its pricing, as did expectations that Moody's would upgrade Metrobank itself.
Korea's Boram Bank signed a US$1.5 billion Global medium term note programme, arranger Merrill Lynch International said on Friday.
It can issue up to US$1.5 billion or its equivalent in other currencies in senior and subordinated notes.
Merrill Lynch Capital Markets Bank Ltd Frankfurt am Main Branch has been appointed as arranger for issues of Deutsche Mark-denominated notes made under the programme.
Hard on the heels of compatriot Sterlite's floating-rate note (FRN) issue on Thursday, Indian television maker Videocon International Ltd entered the U.S. dollar FRN market.
Videocon's three-year US$35 million FRN offered a generous all-in yield of 210 basis points to top-tier managers, bankers said.
They said investors also liked the exposure to Videocon, a leading manufacturer of television products in India.
Videocon's deal has no put or call options.
Peridot Ltd launched a US$20 million three-year FRN guaranteed by Taiwanese computer product-maker Enlight Corp Ltd.
The deal, which includes puts and call options at two years, was issued at par to float at 115 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rate.
The all-in return is about 145 basis points for top tier managers.
